tier_reason: The paper (Vectorized VByte Decoding, ISWAG 2015, arXiv 1503.07387) could not be opened (arXiv and NASA ADS egress-blocked); its abstract, seen only as a WebSearch snippet, says the masked decoder is 2 to 4 times faster than a conventional scalar VByte decoder, and snippet-only paper evidence is capped at C here. The only page actually opened with numbers is the TurboPFor README table (competitor-run, public icapp code, no CPU/flags beside the table), which matches the claimed 9524 vs 4268/4208 MB/s decode row, so C, consistent with the batch-01 verdict on the gh-cpp record for the same project.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Paper abstract (WebSearch snippet only; arXiv blocked): the Masked VByte decoder is 2 to 4 times faster than a conventional scalar VByte decoder. TurboPFor README table (ZIPF 100M ints, 2019.11, competitor-run): MaskedVByte decode 9524 MB/s vs FP_VByte 4268 MB/s and PC_Vbyte 4208 MB/s (about 2.2x, derived from page data); encode 6689 vs 5200 and 2260 MB/s. On gov2.sorted (delta, block 128): MaskedVByte decode 3384 MB/s vs FP_Vbyte 1980 MB/s (about 1.7x, derived from page data).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 131 stars, 20 forks; README lists a third-party Lucene integration (GregBowyer/lucene-solr intrinsics branch) and use by the PISA search engine
corrections.caveats: Tier capped at C: the peer-reviewed paper 'Vectorized VByte Decoding' (ISWAG 2015, arXiv 1503.07387) was not opened (arXiv blocked); its 2-4x claim is known only from the abstract via a search snippet, so a paper-access retier could lift this to B. The repo README has no benchmark numbers. The TurboPFor table is run by a competitor; the README links an i7-6700 / gcc 9.2 benchmark issue (#47) but CPU and flags are not stated next to the table. Same project as the batch-01 record under https://github.com/lemire/maskedvbyte (the lemire URL redirects to fast-pack).

notes: Same project as the batch-01 verdict on https://github.com/lemire/maskedvbyte (confirmed there at C); merge the two ids. Paper abstract says 2-4x, not 3x as the record stated; corrected. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 131 stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-06-07 (active).

tier_reason: Upgraded from B: the README benchmark table compares partitioned VByte indexes against un-partitioned VByte (block_maskedvbyte) on an i7-4790K at 4 GHz under Linux 4.13 / Ubuntu 17.10, the README says the code is built with gcc 7.3.0 at the highest optimization setting and CMakeLists.txt sets -O3 -march=native, and the benchmark code is public (src/create_freq_index.cpp, src/queries.cpp, scripts/). The win is space at equal query speed, not speed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (i7-4790K): VByte docs 10.498 bpi, freqs 8.031 bpi, build 0.704 s, 4.316 microseconds/query; VByte optimal partitioning docs 7.388 bpi, freqs 4.268 bpi, build 0.739 s, 4.378 microseconds/query. That is about 30% (docs) and 47% (freqs) smaller at about 1.4% slower query time (derived from page data); not faster than plain VByte.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 7.3.0 (README: 'tested on Linux Ubuntu with gcc 7.3.0'; table compiled at 'the highest optimization setting'); CMakeLists.txt Release flags -std=c++14 -march=native -O3
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-4790K at 4 GHz, Linux 4.13.0 (Ubuntu 17.10), 64-bit
corrections.caveats: Space win, not a speed win: optimal partitioning cuts docs from 10.498 to 7.388 bpi and freqs from 8.031 to 4.268 bpi, while AND-query time is 4.378 vs 4.316 microseconds (about 1.4% slower, derived from page data). The 'up to 2x better compression with fast decoding' framing comes from the TKDE 2019 paper (arXiv 1804.10949), not opened (arXiv and pages.di.unipi.it blocked). README ties gcc 7.3.0 to testing generally rather than explicitly to the table run. Depends on Boost and ds2i-derived submodules. Last commit 2021-11-10.

notes: Record's caveat that the README gives no CPU or compiler was wrong; they are stated, so tier upgraded to A for the space claim. It is not faster than plain VByte (query time parity, slightly slower); keep only if memory-metric entries are in scope. Metadata checked: MIT, 17 stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2021-11-10 (abandoned, under the >3 years rule).
